summary: Wenatchee NF summit in Yakima County, WA; an L-4 cab built in 1931 and removed or destroyed in 1975; the summit is still reached by road.

facts.design: L-4 cab resting on the ground
facts.status_note: Cab removed in 1975 per the FFLOS register and Willhite (FireLookout.com says destroyed). Willhite's 2020-era captions mention an outhouse still there and a parking area at the summit.

access.note: Willhite says any vehicle with clearance can drive to the summit; where the road gets rough, visitors park and walk. No closure appears in these sources.

visit.trail_note: Willhite lists the hiking distance as drive-up or a 2-mile hike. There is no tower to climb.

events.note: L-4 cab built on the summit, resting on the ground
Panoramic photos taken from the cab's roof; vehicle access existed then and timber was cut to open the north view. One page dates the photos to July 17.
USGS placed a benchmark (TIMBERWOLF MTN LOH); the USGS visited again in 1966 to reference the lookout
Cab removed per the FFLOS register and Willhite; FireLookout.com says destroyed
A new benchmark placed at the site

evidence.supports: L-4 cab built in 1931 as one of many lookouts built for fire protection along the east side of the Cascades; removed in 1975
evidence.quote: This L-4 cab was built in 1931 as one of a long string of lookouts built for fire protection along the east side of the Cascades. It was removed in 1975.

evidence.supports: Built 1931 as an L-4 cab; destroyed 1975 (FireLookout.com)
Cab built 1931 and resting on the ground
evidence.quote: Built in 1931 this was an L-4 cab resting on the ground.

evidence.supports: Panoramics from the roof in 1934; vehicle access at that time; timber cut for the north view
evidence.quote: Panoramics were taken from the roof in 1934. There was vehicle access at that time and a considerable amount of timber had to be cut to get the north view.
The USGS placed a benchmark in 1938 as TIMBERWOLF MTN LOH. They also visited in 1966 referencing the lookout.

evidence.supports: Summit reachable by vehicle with clearance; rough road can be walked
evidence.quote: You can still drive to the top with any vehicle with clearance. If not, park where the road gets rough and hike the road.

evidence.quote: Timberwolf site with Mount Rainier in the distance

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The FFLOS register and Willhite say the cab was removed in 1975; FireLookout.com says destroyed in 1975. The story reports the removal and notes FireLookout.com's wording. No source found says why the cab was removed.

notes_for_editor: Four sites, all volunteer or hobbyist pages; no Forest Service document was read. The removal-versus-destruction wording is unresolved. A SnoWest forum result in search says the cab 'burned in 1975', but that thread returned no readable text, so it is not cited. Access is inferred from Willhite's 2020-era text; check the current road status before publishing the access level. No staffing or fire history was found, so none is written. Footings and foundations were checked on all four pages (full text of the Willhite page; keyword searches of the other three); none is mentioned, so the story states that as a negative finding. The benchmark's location on the summit is not stated in any source, so the story does not say it.
